review.words: For all $n\ge 2k$ the least prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$ is $\le\max(n/k,k)$, with only finitely many exceptions.

import Nodes.«erdos-1094--h3--h3».Context

/-! Hole `h_gr` of a merged partial proof, as a node (D-12 #5, D-29).

theorem erdos_1094__h3__h3 : ∀ (C : ℕ),
  ∃ (K₂ : ℕ),
    ∀ (n k : ℕ),
      K₂ < k →
        k * k ≤ C * (n * Nat.log (2 : ℕ) k) →
          n < k * k → ∃ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p ∧ k < (2 : ℕ) * p ∧ (20 : ℕ) * p < (11 : ℕ) * k ∧ n % p < k % p := by
  sorry
